translation_en: 'Isa ibn Hammad al-Misri narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say, If one of your slave women commits adultery and it is established, let him inflict the prescribed lashes on her without rebuking her. If she does so again, let him inflict the prescribed lashes without rebuking her. If she commits adultery a third time and it is established, let him sell her, even for a rope of hair.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Ibn 'Uyaynah. Another chain: 'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Bursani informed us: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us. Both reported from Ayyub ibn Musa. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar. Another chain: Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to me. Another chain: Hannad ibn al-Sari, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from 'Abdah ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq. All of them reported from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet. Ibn Ishaq's report from Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah says regarding the flogging of a slave woman who commits adultery three times: Then sell her the fourth time.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah al-Qa'nabi narrated to us: Malik narrated to us. Another chain: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us—the wording is his—saying: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah was asked about a slave woman who commits adultery and has not been married. He said: If she commits adultery, flog her; if she does so again, flog her; if she does so again, flog her; then sell her, even for a plaited rope. Ibn Shihab said: I do not know whether that is after the third or fourth time. In al-Qa'nabi's report Ibn Shihab explained that a plaited rope means a cord.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: I heard Malik say: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, that the Messenger of Allah was asked about a slave woman. They related a report like theirs, but did not mention Ibn Shihab's explanation that the plaited rope is a cord.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Salih. Another chain: 'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us. Both reported from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubaydullah, from Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, from the Prophet, with the like of Malik's hadith. Both chains are uncertain whether she is sold after the third or fourth time.

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us: Sulayman Abu Dawud narrated to us: Za'idah narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: 'Ali addressed the people: O people, carry out the prescribed punishment on your enslaved men and women, whether or not they have been married. A slave woman belonging to the Messenger of Allah committed adultery, and he ordered me to flog her. She had only recently given birth, and I feared that if I flogged her I would kill her. I told the Prophet about this, and he said, You did well.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: Yahya ibn Adam informed us: Isra'il narrated to us, from al-Suddi, with this chain. He did not mention whether they had been married or not. He added in the report: Leave her until she recovers.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Qatadah report from Anas ibn Malik that a man who had drunk wine was brought to the Prophet, who flogged him with two palm branches about forty times. Abu Bakr did the same. When it was 'Umar's time, he consulted the people. 'Abd al-Rahman said, The lightest prescribed punishment is eighty. 'Umar ordered that amount.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid, meaning Ibn al-Harith, narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us: I heard Anas say that a man was brought to the Messenger of Allah. He related something like it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that Allah's Prophet flogged for drinking wine with palm branches and sandals. Abu Bakr then flogged forty times. When 'Umar came to power and people had moved into the countryside and villages, he asked what they thought about flogging for wine. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said, I think you should make it like the lightest prescribed punishment. 'Umar then flogged eighty times.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us with this chain, with the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet used to flog for wine with sandals and palm branches forty times. He then mentioned a report like theirs, but did not mention the countryside and villages.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us; they said: Isma'il, Ibn 'Ulayyah, narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from 'Abdullah al-Danaj. Another chain: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali—the wording is his—informed us: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Fayruz, the freedman of Ibn 'Amir al-Danaj, narrated to us: Hudayn ibn al-Mundhir Abu Sasan narrated to us. He said: I was present with 'Uthman ibn 'Affan when al-Walid was brought after he had prayed the dawn prayer as two units, then asked, Shall I add more for you? Two men testified against him: one, Humran, testified that he drank wine, and another said he saw him vomit. 'Uthman said, He would not have vomited unless he had drunk it. He said, 'Ali, stand and flog him. 'Ali said, Hasan, stand and flog him. Hasan said, Let the one who took its sweetness bear its bitterness. He seemed displeased with him, so 'Uthman said, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far, stand and flog him. He flogged him while 'Ali counted, until he reached forty; then 'Ali said, Stop. He said: The Prophet flogged forty, Abu Bakr flogged forty, and 'Umar flogged eighty. Each is a Sunnah, and this is dearer to me. 'Ali ibn Hujr adds that Isma'il said: I heard the report of al-Danaj from him, but did not retain it.

Muhammad ibn Minhal al-Darir narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Abu Hasin, from 'Umayr ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali, who said: Whenever I carried out a prescribed punishment on someone and he died from it, I felt no misgiving except in the case of the wine drinker. If he died, I would pay compensation for him, because the Messenger of Allah did not establish a fixed rule for it.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us with this chain, with the like of it.

Ahmad ibn 'Isa narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Amr informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, who said: While we were with Sulayman ibn Yasar, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir came and spoke to him. Sulayman turned to us and said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir narrated to me, from his father, from Abu Burdah al-Ansari, that he heard the Messenger of Allah say: No one is to be flogged with more than ten lashes except for one of Allah's prescribed punishments.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Numayr all narrated from Ibn 'Uyaynah; the wording is 'Amr's. He said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah in a gathering. He said: Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, commit adultery, steal, or kill a life Allah has forbidden except with right. Whoever among you fulfills this will have his reward from Allah. Whoever commits any of these acts and is punished for it, that punishment is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of them and Allah conceals it, his affair is with Allah: if He wills, He will pardon him, and if He wills, He will punish him.

'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain, and added that he recited to us the verse from Surat al-Nisa' 60:12: that they should not associate anything with Allah, and the rest of the verse.

Isma'il ibn Salim narrated to me: Hushaym informed us: Khalid informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah took our pledge as he took the women's pledge: that we would not associate anything with Allah, steal, commit adultery, kill our children, or slander one another. Whoever among you fulfills this will have his reward from Allah. Whoever commits an offense and its punishment is carried out on him, it is an expiation for him. Whoever Allah conceals, his affair is with Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from al-Sunabihi, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I was one of the leaders who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah. We pledged that we would not associate anything with Allah, commit adultery, steal, kill a life Allah has forbidden except with right, plunder, or disobey. If we did any of that, the judgment would rest with Allah. Ibn Rumh said: His judgment would rest with Allah.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah to hear and obey in hardship and ease, in eagerness and reluctance, and when others were given preference over us; not to dispute authority with its rightful holders; and to speak the truth wherever we were, fearing no blame for Allah's sake.

Ibn Numayr narrated this to us: 'Abdullah, meaning Ibn Idris, narrated to us: Ibn 'Ajlan, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, and Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid, with this chain, with the like of it.

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz, meaning al-Darawardi, narrated to us, from Yazid, Ibn al-Had, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from his father. My father narrated to me that we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah with a report like Ibn Idris's hadith.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb ibn Muslim narrated to us: my uncle 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Bukayr narrated to me, from Busr ibn Sa'id, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah, who said: We entered upon 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit while he was ill and asked him to tell us a beneficial hadith he had heard from the Messenger of Allah. He said: The Messenger of Allah summoned us and we pledged allegiance to him. Among what he required was that we pledge to hear and obey in times of energy and reluctance, hardship and ease, and when others were given preference over us, and not to dispute authority with its rightful holders. He said: Except if you see manifest disbelief for which you have clear proof from Allah.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us; they said: al-Layth informed us. Another chain: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Injury caused by an animal is without liability; injury caused by a well is without liability; injury caused by a mine is without liability; and one fifth is due on buried treasure.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad all narrated from Ibn 'Uyaynah. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Ishaq, meaning Ibn 'Isa, narrated to us: Malik narrated to us. Both reported from al-Zuhri with al-Layth's chain, with the like of his hadith.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab and 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, with the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from al-Aswad ibn al-'Ala', from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Injury caused by a well is without liability; injury caused by a mine is without liability; injury caused by an animal is without liability; and one fifth is due on buried treasure.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salam al-Jumahi narrated to us: al-Rabi', meaning Ibn Muslim, narrated to us. Another chain: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us. Another chain: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. They said: Shu'bah narrated to us. Both reported from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with the like of it.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet said: If people were given things merely on the basis of their claims, some would claim the lives and property of others. Rather, the oath is required of the one against whom the claim is made.
